scope.held: 160 heads; RNG consumption/order; speed28m/s; drag0.74/s; each native I, radius, seed, life10.2..12.7s; colour; all rocket/event/height/envelope values; reference scale. Only the native initial direction vector changes.
scope.integration: Midpoint emitted reference candela seconds, all heads before water clipping; fractions cancel any single common thermal-greybody area multiplier. Not radiant energy or burn safety.
scope.clearance: World-space head centres against native water cutoff y=0.03m. No terrain, flame radius, fragments, people, buildings or actual pyrotechnic safety modelling. Threshold endpoints solved on continuous envelope; no cadence dependence.
scope.direction: Uniform y in[-1,1] is equal-area spherical polar sampling with the same deterministic golden-angle azimuth. The finite realization is not a perfect shell or a measured real willow.

analyticAllRandomBound80.explanation: Worst possible native RNG support: y=-1, life=12.7s, zero vertical carrier velocity at apex, zero vertical wind. Longer life reaches the envelope thresholds later. Head centres only; not safety certification.

analyticAllRandomBoundUi78.explanation: Worst possible native RNG support: y=-1, life=12.7s, zero vertical carrier velocity at apex, zero vertical wind. Longer life reaches the envelope thresholds later. Head centres only; not safety certification.
analyticAllRandomBoundUi78.note: ui.js/index.html default78deg differs from physics default80deg. At the all-RNG support endpoint the native water cutoff can remove an already effectively extinguished final star; this is not a zero-collision proof.

limits: One photograph or an un-timestamped video screenshot cannot identify an exact shell family, physical size, velocity or camera exposure.
A spherical long-tail candidate is defensible, but willow is an effect family, not a universal sphere constraint.
This audit neither admits the candidate to runtime nor proves its GPU appearance, performance, smoke mass, collisions or user acceptance.
